A field of experiments · 2026

Experiments used to be expensive.Now they cost a weekend.

So I run a lot of them. Everything here is an idea I gave a night or two, most built solo in spare hours. The barrier to trying something didn't move. It disappeared.

The person behind the index

I build software that questions its own foundation.

I'm Chris Kluis. For nearly two decades I've worked the seam where product, marketing, and go-to-market meet in B2B SaaS. I took an enterprise software company from on-prem to SaaS to acquisition, and co-founded SaaSRock. Back then I was the idea guy; a developer built everything.

The tooling changed that. Everything here is me building the ideas I used to have to give away, and an open invitation for every other idea person to start experimenting too.

03

Agent tools

Making agents cheaper, better reviewed, and easier to steer.

4
  1. batonv7.5 one thread that never fills up Shipped 0 0 ↗
    baton v7.5Shipped

    What if the orchestrator never read a file, and its thread lasted as long as the work did?

    A Claude Code mod. During a run the prime may only dispatch, ask and use its memory; a guard refuses everything else. Sub-orchestrators run each phase and hand back one line of at most 280 bytes, noted into a memory the prime can zoom into. Rulings you give stick across runs, irreversible commands from any agent wait for you, and every behavior change lands red, green, blue. Underneath is still the router prompt and its record: evidence that cites, verdicts per criterion, gates a person holds, and TEAM: github for a team.

    0 files the prime reads≤280 B back from a phase27 hooks
    Claude Code modJavaScriptMulti-agentupdated Oct 5, 2026
    Live ↗Code ↗Changelog ↗v6 ↗

  4. workflowForge paste a workflow, get a page you can send Shipped 0 0 ↗
    workflowForgeShipped

    What if any workflow could become a diagram you can send — one where no two lines ever cross?
